items.meaning: to cause something to happen, often a change
items.example: Stricter recycling laws could bring about a real shift in how households deal with waste.

items.meaning: to reduce the amount of something you use or do
items.example: I've been trying to cut down on screen time before bed because it affects my sleep.

items.meaning: to stop using something gradually over a period of time
items.example: Many cities plan to phase out petrol cars by the end of the next decade.

items.meaning: to do or complete a task, study or piece of research
items.example: Researchers carried out a survey of 2,000 commuters to measure travel habits.

items.meaning: to form a particular part or proportion of a total
items.example: Renewable sources accounted for roughly a third of electricity generation in 2020.

items.meaning: to stop doing something, especially a habit
items.example: My uncle gave up smoking after his doctor warned him about his lungs.

items.meaning: to investigate or examine a problem or possibility
items.example: The council has promised to look into complaints about noise from the new airport.

items.meaning: to start a business, organisation or system
items.example: After graduating, my cousin set up a small online shop selling handmade bags.

items.meaning: to start a new hobby, activity or job
items.example: I took up photography last year, and now I take my camera everywhere.

items.meaning: to stay at the same level or pace as someone or something
items.example: Older workers sometimes struggle to keep up with rapid changes in technology.

items.meaning: to depend on someone or something
items.example: Rural communities often rely on a single bus route to reach hospitals and schools.

items.meaning: to take action to solve a problem or handle a situation
items.example: Governments need long-term plans to deal with rising housing costs.

items.meaning: to draw attention to a fact or detail
items.example: Critics point out that online courses rarely offer the same support as classrooms.

items.meaning: to decide that something is not possible or suitable
items.example: The minister did not rule out raising fuel taxes to reduce congestion.

items.meaning: to cause a particular outcome or situation
items.example: Poor diet in childhood can result in health problems later in life.

items.meaning: to be caused by or originate from something
items.example: Much of the stress students feel stems from pressure to achieve top grades.

items.meaning: to go to someone or something for help or advice
items.example: When I'm stuck on a maths problem, I usually turn to my older sister.

items.meaning: to think of an idea, plan or solution
items.example: Our team came up with a simple app to help neighbours share tools.

items.meaning: to delay doing something until later
items.example: I tend to put off revising until the week before an exam, which isn't ideal.

items.meaning: to communicate an idea so that people understand it
items.example: Good teachers can get across difficult concepts using everyday examples.

items.meaning: to do something you have not had time to do earlier
items.example: At weekends I catch up on sleep and the reading I missed during the week.

items.meaning: to fail to make progress at the same rate as others
items.example: Children without internet access at home can fall behind their classmates.

items.meaning: to end someone's employment, usually because there is not enough work
items.example: The factory laid off two hundred staff after automating its assembly line.

items.meaning: to take control of something, such as a company or role
items.example: Machines have taken over many repetitive tasks in modern warehouses.

items.meaning: to use all of something so that none is left
items.example: If we keep using groundwater at this rate, some regions may run out of it.

items.meaning: to begin a journey
items.example: We set off before sunrise so we could reach the mountains by lunchtime.

items.meaning: to feel pleased and excited about something that will happen
items.example: I'm really looking forward to travelling abroad once my exams are over.

items.meaning: to experience a difficult period or event
items.example: Many families went through financial hardship during the economic downturn.

items.meaning: to deal successfully with a difficult situation
items.example: Hospitals struggled to cope with the number of patients during the heatwave.

items.meaning: to choose one thing instead of another
items.example: More young people are opting for vocational courses rather than university degrees.
